articles.author: Node & Neural
articles.description:
Your AI agent just quoted a contract to a customer. That contract was terminated six weeks ago and deleted from Postgres the same day. Its embedding wasn't. It was still sitting in a separate vector database, and nobody owned the sync job.
  
  



  
  
  Two databases, one sync job



Most RAG tutorials start the same way: documents live in Postgres, and their embeddings go to a dedicated vector database. Two systems means a sync job. Every insert, update and delete has to reach both, in order, or your agent retrieves things that no longer exist.
It also means two security models. Postgres knows this user can only see their own company's contracts. The vector database doesn't, so permissions get copied into metadata filters, and the copies drift. And every question pays two round trips: …
articles.title: Your RAG Agent Is Quoting Deleted Documents (Postgres + pgvector Fix)

articles.author: D4nix1
articles.description:
I Built an Experimental APK/IPA Analysis Tool — I’d Love Your Honest Feedback!
Hi everyone!
I’ve been working on a project called CrossPlatform App Converter, currently at version 0.15.0 (Experimental), and I’d like to invite developers and curious testers to give it a try.
The project is a Windows tool designed to analyze Android APK and iOS IPA packages and generate experimental materials that may help with manual cross-platform reconstruction.
What I’d like you to test
I’m looking for honest feedback, especially:
Bugs, crashes, and unexpected behavior.
Installation or compatibility issues.
Incorrect or incomplete analysis results.
Confusing interface elements or poor user experience.
Missing features or useful improvements.
Anything that simply feels poorly designed or implemented.
Please don’t hold back on criticism! I want to know what is wrong with my project, what doesn’t make sense, what could be improved, and even what you think should be redesigned from scratch.
Important limitations
This is an early experimental project. It does not automatically convert Android apps into fully functional iOS apps, or vice versa.
The generated materials are experimental starting points and require manual development, review, compilation, and testing. Bugs, incomplete results, and compatibility problems are expected.
Where to find it
GitHub repository and Windows installer:
https://github.com/D4nix1/CrossPlatform-App-Converter
How to share feedback
You can:
Open an issue on GitHub.
Suggest improvements.
Share your experience in the comments below.
Please include the steps to reproduce a bug whenever possible. That makes it much easier to investigate and fix.
I’m collecting community feedback throughout November and early December to help guide the next development cycle.
Thank you to anyone willing to test it, criticize it, or suggest improvements. Even negative feedback is valuable!
I’d rather have an honest list of problems than a hundred empty compliments.
articles.title: I Built an Experimental APK/IPA Analysis Tool — Looking for Honest Feedback!

Long agent runs change how you use a Mac. You spend less time typing code and more time waiting, copying output, juggling windows, and wondering whether you have quota left.
These are the small fixes that made that loop smoother for me. Most are built into macOS or free. Pick the three you don't know yet.
caffeinate before a long run


If your Mac sleeps mid-task, the agent stops too. Run caffeinate -dis in a spare terminal tab and macOS won't sleep until you press Control-C. Or wrap a single command: caffeinate -i npm test.
Append ; say done to any slow command: npm run build; say done. Now you can go read docs and hear when it finishes instead of checking every minute.

articles.description:
A Zimbra CVE-2026-10632 Response Checklist for Security and Mail Teams


CVE-2026-10632 is a cross-team issue. Security teams see the XSS and CVE-2026-50053 chain. Mail administrators know which Zimbra builds and browser routes are running. User support knows which Classic Web Client workflows cannot be interrupted. A response that leaves those groups working separately tends to miss either the vulnerable path or the business impact.
The technical facts are compact. The flaw is in the Classic Web Client /h/rest document editor. The packages parameter reaches script attributes without HTML encoding. CVE-2026-50053 adds request-attribute override behavior, letting a crafted URL run JavaScript in another signed-in user's session. The attacker needs an ordinary account and the victim must open…
articles.title: A Zimbra CVE-2026-10632 Response Checklist for Security and Mail Teams

articles.author: KolmoPDF
articles.description:
A retrieval result can contain the correct sentence and still send a reader to the wrong page. One common cause is a document pipeline that concatenates extracted text, splits it into chunks, and calculates citations afterward. Once the page boundaries are gone, matching a chunk back to the PDF becomes guesswork, especially when headers and repeated phrases appear on several pages.
Keep page references attached to extracted blocks before chunking. Then carry those references forward when blocks are merged. This also gives an evaluator somewhere concrete to look when a retrieved answer is wrong.
Imagine a report whose final paragraph on page 4 continues on page 5:
Page 4: The device operates at a maximum pressure of
Page 5: 12 bar when the ambient temperature is below 40 C.

A useful chunk …
articles.title: PDF RAG citations break when chunks lose page boundaries

Ana asks her agent to rename priceWithTax to grossPrice, and it renames every caller it can find. At the same moment Bea asks her agent for a new POST /invoices endpoint. Her agent reads the billing module, sees priceWithTax, and writes a new file that calls it.
The two agents never touched the same file, so git merges both without complaint, and the build is broken until someone runs it. Neither agent had any way to know the other existed. That's the problem I started building Lanes for.
Lanes is a small server plus a hook for each agent.
Before an agent edits a file, it takes a lease. If a s…

articles.author: Sneha S
articles.description:
StudyPilot AI: Making Exam Preparation Smarter


Preparing for exams isn't just about studying hard. It's also about managing time, organizing subjects, tracking progress, and staying consistent.
That's the problem I wanted to solve with StudyPilot AI — a student-focused study-planning application designed to make exam preparation more organized and manageable.
Students often struggle with:
Managing multiple subjects and exam dates.
Creating realistic study schedules.
Tracking completed study sessions.
Handling missed study sessions.
Maintaining consistency during exam preparation.
StudyPilot AI aims to simplify exam preparation through structured study planning and progress tracking.
The idea is to help students organize their preparation based on their exam dates and subjects.
1. Exam-Based Planning
Organize study preparation around exam dates and subjects.
2. Structured Study Schedules
Create study schedules to make preparation more organized.
3. Progress Tracking
Mark completed study sessions and keep track of preparation progress.
4. Intelligent Rescheduling
Missed a planned study session? Reschedule it without losing previously completed progress.
5. Local Progress Persistence
Keep study progress saved locally so students can continue their preparation.
As an Electronics and Communication Engineering student interested in AI, Machine Learning, and software development, I wanted to work on a problem that students experience in their everyday academic lives.
Instead of creating another generic productivity tool, I wanted to explore a solution focused specifically on exam preparation.
I look forward to improving StudyPilot AI, exploring additional intelligent capabilities, and making it more useful for students.
GitHub Repository:

https://github.com/snehassneha4578-collab/StudyPilot-AI
I'd love to hear your feedback, suggestions, and ideas!
Building technology that makes learning more manageable. One study session at a time. 🚀
articles.title: StudyPilot AI: Building a Smarter Study Planner for Students 🚀
